title: Vulval and vaginal disorders: VIN, lichen sclerosus, Paget disease, vulval cancer and DES exposure
subject: ss-obg
refs: Gynecology by Ten Teachers 21e Ch 13 (Benign conditions of the vulva and vagina), Ch 16 (Premalignant and malignant disease)
FIGO Cancer Report: Cancer of the vulva (2021 update)
British Association of Dermatologists guidelines for the management of lichen sclerosus (2018)

steps.say: Vulval squamous intraepithelial neoplasia exhibits two distinct pathogenic pathways with differing oncogenic risks. Usual-type VIN is caused by persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus 16 and 18 in younger women, whereas differentiated VIN is HPV-negative, developing in postmenopausal women with chronic lichen sclerosus.
steps.tx: **Vulval intraepithelial neoplasia** divides into 2 biological pathways: **usual-type VIN** (HPV-associated, driven by genotypes 16 and 18, presenting as multifocal lesions in younger smokers) and **differentiated VIN** (dVIN, HPV-negative, arising on a background of **lichen sclerosus** with TP53 mutations, carrying a high rapid malignant progression rate).

steps.say: Lichen sclerosus is a chronic lymphocytic inflammatory dermatosis that causes severe scarring and anatomical distortion. Patients present with severe intractable pruritus vulvae and characteristic porcelain-white parchment patches arranged in a figure-of-eight distribution around the vulva and anus.
steps.tx: **Lichen sclerosus** is an autoimmune dermatosis of the vulva and perineum characterized by intractable **pruritus vulvae**. Examination reveals thinning, **porcelain-white** atrophic plaques in a classic **figure-of-eight** perivulvar and perianal distribution, with progressive resorption of the labia minora and clitoral phimosis.

left.title: Clinical Hallmarks of Lichen Sclerosus
points: Intractable pruritus vulvae, dyspareunia, and dysuria
Figure-of-eight distribution around introitus and anus

right.title: Architectural Distortion & Risk
points: Resorption and fusion of labia minora
Phimosis and burying of the clitoral glans
3 to 5 percent lifetime risk of squamous cell carcinoma

steps.say: Superpotent topical corticosteroids represent the undisputed first-line therapy for vulval lichen sclerosus. Applying clobetasol propionate zero point zero five percent ointment daily relieves chronic pruritus, restores epithelial texture, and decreases progression to invasive squamous cell carcinoma.
steps.tx: First-line medical therapy for vulval lichen sclerosus requires **superpotent topical steroids**, specifically **clobetasol propionate 0.05% ointment** applied daily for one month, tapering over 3 months to an intermittent maintenance schedule to suppress dermal T-cell inflammation and lower the lifetime risk of progression to squamous carcinoma.

rows: Halts dermal T-cell lymphocytic band inflammation
Promotes tissue healing and resolves hyperkeratosis
Once or twice weekly as required
Prevents symptom relapse and architectural fusion

steps.say: Extramammary Paget disease of the vulva presents as a slow-growing, highly pruritic neoplastic intraepithelial plaque. Lesions display a classic velvety erythematous weeping plaque with scattered white porcelain islands, termed a strawberries and cream appearance, containing mucin-positive Paget cells.
steps.tx: **Extramammary Paget disease** presents as an eczematoid, erythematous, velvety plaque studded with white islands (**strawberries and cream** appearance) accompanied by intense pruritus. Histopathology demonstrates large, pale **Paget cells** containing mucin that stain intensely positive for periodic acid-Schiff and cytokeratin 7.

nodes.label: Identify pruritic eczematous velvety lesion of the labia majora
Perform full-thickness punch biopsy of the erythematous plaque
Demonstrate large PAS-positive, mucicarmine-positive Paget cells
Screen for concurrent gastrointestinal or urological adenocarcinoma (15 to 20%)

steps.say: Vulval carcinoma is predominantly squamous cell carcinoma staged under the updated FIGO 2021 system. Staging depends on primary tumor dimensions, measured depth of stromal invasion exceeding one millimeter, and the presence and morphology of inguinofemoral lymph node metastases.
steps.tx: Primary **vulval carcinoma** (over 90 percent squamous cell carcinoma) is staged according to the **FIGO 2021 staging** system. Stromal invasion depth > 1 mm defines invasion; staging integrates tumor size, adjacent tissue extension, and the number, size, and extracapsular spread of **inguinofemoral lymph node** metastases.

rows: Tumor > 2 cm or any size with deep invasion
Extension to lower 1/3 of urethra, vagina, anus
Any size tumor with local spread
Any size tumor with local spread
Any size tumor with nodal spread
Lymph node metastasis with extracapsular spread

steps.say: Surgical treatment of Stage IB invasive vulval carcinoma requires radical excision with confirmed oncological clear margins. Radical wide local excision achieves a one-centimeter macroscopic surgical margin, combined with ipsilateral or bilateral inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy through separate incisions.
steps.tx: Standard operative management for **Stage IB** vulval cancer entails **radical local excision** with a 1 cm gross clinical margin (aiming for > 8 mm microscopic margin) combined with inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy performed via separate groin incisions ('triple incision technique') to minimize wound breakdown.

left.title: Radical Wide Local Excision
points: 1 cm gross macroscopic surgical margin around tumor
Resection carried down to deep perineal fascia
Provides equivalent local control to radical vulvectomy with less morbidity

right.title: Inguinofemoral Lymphadenectomy
points: Removes superficial and deep femoral lymph nodes below cribriform fascia
Bilateral groin dissection mandatory for midline lesions

steps.say: Sentinel lymph node biopsy offers a minimally invasive alternative to complete groin dissection in selected early vulval carcinomas. Technetium-99m radiocolloid and blue dye localization in unifocal tumors smaller than four centimeters avoids complete lymphadenectomy, dramatically decreasing lower limb lymphedema.
steps.tx: **Sentinel lymph node** biopsy using **technetium-99m** radiocolloid and isosulfan blue dye is validated for unifocal vulval tumors < 4 cm with clinically negative groins (GROINSS-V study). It provides high diagnostic accuracy while drastically reducing the incidence of debilitating chronic **lower limb lymphedema**.

nodes.label: Identify unifocal primary vulval tumor < 4 cm with negative clinical groin nodes
Peritumoral intradermal injection of Tc-99m nanocolloid and patent blue dye
Intraoperative gamma probe detection and visualization of blue-stained sentinel nodes
Pathological ultrastaging: negative sentinel node spares full inguinofemoral dissection

steps.say: Prenatal maternal exposure to diethylstilbestrol taken to prevent miscarriage is historically associated with rare genital tract clear cell adenocarcinoma. Exposed daughters develop adenosis of the upper vagina and cervix, structural vaginal cockscomb ridges, and clear cell malignancies in young adulthood.
steps.tx: In-utero exposure to **diethylstilbestrol** (DES), historically prescribed to prevent threatened miscarriage, leads to vaginal adenosis, structural uterine T-shaped anomalies, and a 40-fold increased risk of developing rare **clear cell adenocarcinoma** of the vagina and cervix in young adult daughters exposed before 18 weeks.
